reason: Phagocytes are shown engulfing debris near the cut, so they are a plausible first step in wound repair.
expectation: The phagocytes will clear debris from the wound.

effect: Phagocytes cleared debris, revealing supply, surface and support slots for the healing wound.
reaction: The distinction between clearing the wound and rebuilding it is clear.
reason: Repair signals point toward the nearby vessel, suggesting they can help establish the wound's blood supply.
expectation: The signals will stimulate a vessel response that helps supply the wound.

effect: The repair signals produced a capillary sprout connected to the existing circulation, which may fill the wound’s supply slot.
reaction: The connected parent vessel makes the source of the new supply clear.
reason: The sprout is a plausible fit for the healing wound’s supply slot.
expectation: The capillary sprout will supply the healing wound.

effect: The capillary sprout fills the supply slot and forms a connected flow route to the wound.
reaction: The completed loop makes the new blood supply easy to follow.
reason: RNA building blocks are shown entering the fibroblast nucleus, suggesting the next step toward making wound-supporting collagen.
expectation: The fibroblasts will make an RNA message for collagen production.

effect: The fibroblasts now have collagen messenger RNA at their ribosomes, ready for protein production.
reaction: The picture clearly separates the retained DNA from its RNA copy.
reason: Matrix nutrients include amino acids, which fibroblasts need to build collagen from the RNA instructions.
expectation: The fibroblasts will use the nutrients to make collagen for wound support.

effect: The fibroblasts made and exported collagen fibres, producing connective tissue for wound support.
reaction: The sequence connects RNA instructions to extracellular collagen clearly.
reason: The new connective tissue appears suited to the wound’s support slot.
expectation: The connective tissue will provide support in the healing wound.

effect: The new connective tissue fills the support slot, though the young tissue is not yet as strong as uninjured skin.
reaction: The strength limitation is a useful distinction.
reason: The epidermal edge cells and their nutrients suggest a way to rebuild the remaining surface.
expectation: The nourished edge cells will grow or spread to help close the wound surface.

effect: The edge cells produced a new epidermal surface that can fill the remaining wound slot.
reaction: The sheet extending across the gap makes the closure clear.
reason: The new surface matches the healing skin’s remaining surface slot.
expectation: The new epidermal sheet will close the wound surface.

effect: The new surface closes the gap, completing the wound’s surface, support and supply goal; the clot still needs clearing.
reaction: The distinction between surface closure and deeper strengthening is useful.
reason: Clot-clearing enzymes are shown breaking down fibrin, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: The enzymes will break down the temporary fibrin clot.

effect: The enzymes cleared most of the temporary fibrin, completing the remaining goal while leaving a still-maturing scar.
reaction: The distinction between clot removal and continued tissue maturation is useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making collagen from a gene’s RNA copy and adding it as wound support connected familiar cell biology to tissue repair. The planned pictures trace the process clearly.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting each completed component into the wound was predictable and somewhat repetitive, although it made the three repair requirements clear.

surprise.text: The capillary sprout joined another vessel to form a local flow route, rather than simply ending at the wound.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though combining cell nutrients directly with edge cells simplified the processes behind surface closure.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the repair sequence tied molecular events to a visible outcome, while acknowledging that closed skin is still gaining strength.
